usage: bitable_schema.py export [-h] [--base-token BASE_TOKEN]
                                [--tables TABLES] --out OUT
                                [--lark-cli LARK_CLI] [--profile PROFILE]
                                [--identity {bot,user}]

Snapshot a tenant base's table/field structure to a committed manifest (name-
keyed, no IDs).

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --base-token BASE_TOKEN
                        source base token (default: $FEISHU_PHASE2_BASE_TOKEN)
  --tables TABLES       comma-separated table names to export; omit for the
                        whole base
  --out OUT             manifest output path (committed)
  --lark-cli LARK_CLI
  --profile PROFILE     lark-cli config profile to route through (e.g. a
                        separate prod-tenant login; dev's default profile is
                        left untouched)
  --identity {bot,user}
                        lark-cli token identity (default: bot; cross-tenant
                        writes usually need 'user', the base owner's token)

parity-help.stdout:
usage: bitable_schema.py parity [-h] --source-base SOURCE_BASE --target-base
                                TARGET_BASE [--tables TABLES]
                                [--ignore-table-prefix PREFIX]
                                [--ignore-table NAME]
                                [--table-alias SOURCE=TARGET]
                                [--ignore-field TABLE.FIELD]
                                [--fail-on {any,missing}]
                                [--lark-cli LARK_CLI] [--profile PROFILE]
                                [--identity {bot,user}]

Read-only: report structure differences between a SOURCE tenant (e.g. dev) and
a TARGET tenant (e.g. prod). Exit 1 if the target lags/diverges — usable as a
CI parity gate.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --source-base SOURCE_BASE
                        reference tenant base token (e.g. dev)
  --target-base TARGET_BASE
                        tenant to check (e.g. prod)
  --tables TABLES       comma-separated table names; omit for the whole base
  --ignore-table-prefix PREFIX
                        drop SOURCE tables whose name starts with PREFIX
                        (repeatable; e.g. dev scratch '99_')
  --ignore-table NAME   drop a SOURCE table by exact name (repeatable; e.g.
                        'QC_Report')
  --table-alias SOURCE=TARGET
                        compare a SOURCE table against an intentionally
                        renamed TARGET table (repeatable)
  --ignore-field TABLE.FIELD
                        ignore an explicitly retired/replaced SOURCE field
                        (repeatable; exact TABLE.FIELD)
  --fail-on {any,missing}
                        exit 1 on 'any' divergence (default) or only on
                        'missing' tables/fields (drift still reported but not
                        failed — for a prod-lag alert where dev may carry
                        extra/dirty options)
  --lark-cli LARK_CLI
  --profile PROFILE     lark-cli config profile to route through (e.g. a
                        separate prod-tenant login; dev's default profile is
                        left untouched)
  --identity {bot,user}
                        lark-cli token identity (default: bot; cross-tenant
                        writes usually need 'user', the base owner's token)

seed-import-help.stdout:
usage: bitable_schema.py seed-import [-h] --base-token BASE_TOKEN --table
                                     TABLE --seed SEED --key KEY [--write]
                                     [--yes] [--prune] [--lark-cli LARK_CLI]
                                     [--profile PROFILE]
                                     [--identity {bot,user}]

Idempotently upsert a seed CSV into a TARGET table's rows, matched by --key.
Dry-run unless --write.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --base-token BASE_TOKEN
                        TARGET (e.g. prod) base token
  --table TABLE         reference table name
  --seed SEED           seed CSV path (e.g. bitable_schema/seed/<table>.csv)
  --key KEY             business-key column(s) to match rows by; comma-
                        separated for a composite key (e.g. 'Row_key,规格书字段')
  --write               apply the upserts (else dry-run plan)
  --yes                 confirm the TARGET base is correct; REQUIRED together
                        with --write
  --prune               also DELETE target rows whose key is absent from the
                        seed (destructive)
  --lark-cli LARK_CLI
  --profile PROFILE     lark-cli config profile to route through (e.g. a
                        separate prod-tenant login; dev's default profile is
                        left untouched)
  --identity {bot,user}
                        lark-cli token identity (default: bot; cross-tenant
                        writes usually need 'user', the base owner's token)

promote-help.stdout:
usage: bitable_schema.py promote [-h] --manifest MANIFEST [--seeds SEEDS]
                                 --base-token BASE_TOKEN [--write] [--yes]
                                 [--prune] [--lark-cli LARK_CLI]
                                 [--profile PROFILE] [--identity {bot,user}]

One dev->prod step: apply structure + seed reference data + print the env
delta, self-gated by a re-check. Dry-run unless --write.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --manifest MANIFEST   structure manifest (bitable_schema/manifest.json)
  --seeds SEEDS         seed registry JSON listing reference tables/csv/key
                        (default: bitable_schema/seeds.json)
  --base-token BASE_TOKEN
                        TARGET (e.g. prod) base token
  --write               apply structure + seeds (else dry-run plan)
  --yes                 confirm the TARGET base is correct; REQUIRED together
                        with --write
  --prune               seed-import: delete target rows whose key is absent
                        from the seed (destructive)
  --lark-cli LARK_CLI
  --profile PROFILE     lark-cli config profile to route through (e.g. a
                        separate prod-tenant login; dev's default profile is
                        left untouched)
  --identity {bot,user}
                        lark-cli token identity (default: bot; cross-tenant
                        writes usually need 'user', the base owner's token)
